question:
A 36-year-old female presents with a three-month history of loose stools (3-4 times daily), abdominal
pain, and occasional palpitations. She reports irritability, poor sleep, and unintentional weight loss of 6
pounds in one month. Her medical history includes asthma managed with albuterol as needed, and she
takes oral contraceptives. Physical examination reveals tachycardia (104/min), low blood pressure

(95/65 mmHg), a symmetrically enlarged non-tender thyroid with an audible bruit, exophthalmos, and
hyperreflexia. Laboratory results show: Serum: - Na+: 140 mEq/L - K+: 4.1 mEq/L - Cl-: 104 mEq/L -
HCO3-: 26 mEql/L - BUN: 18 mg/dL - Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL - Hemoglobin: 14.0 g/dL - Leukocytes:
7,400/mm^3 - Platelets: 450,000/mm^3 Urine pregnancy test is negative. After initiating symptomatic
relief medication, what is the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A)
Methimazole (B) Hydrocortisone (C) Propylthiouracil (D) Radioactive iodine therapy (E) Observation
and close monitoring (F) Thyroid suppression therapy (G) Lugol's solution (H) Plasmapheresis (I)
Surgical thyroidectomy (J) Beta-blocker therapy alone
 A. Plasmapheresis
B. Propylthiouracil
C. Hydrocortisone
D. Radioactive iodine therapy
E. Beta-blocker therapy alone
F. Lugol's solution
G. Thyroid suppression therapy
H. Methimazole
I. Surgical thyroidectomy
J. Observation and close monitoring
